title: Directed colimits of ring sheaves compute the underlying module colimit on a site
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site essentially small in a coefficient universe $w$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of unital commutative rings on it. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed poset in $w$ and let $(A_i,a_{ij})_{i\leq j}$ be a diagram of sheaves of unital commutative rings, with compatible unital ring-sheaf maps $s_i:R\to A_i$, so $a_{ij}s_i=s_j$. Suppose a cocone of unital ring-sheaf maps $q_i:A_i\to A$ is a colimit in the category of sheaves of unital commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and a unital map $s:R\to A$ satisfies $q_i s_i=s$ for every $i$. Give $A_i$ and $A$ their $R$-module sheaf structures by $r\cdot x=s_i(r)x$ and $r\cdot x=s(r)x$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then the underlying $R$-module sheaf $A$, with these same maps $q_i$, is a colimit of the underlying $R$-module sheaves $A_i$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Explicitly, for every $R$-module sheaf $M$ and compatible $R$-linear maps $f_i:A_i\to M$, there is a unique $R$-linear map $f:A\to M$ with $f q_i=f_i$ for every $i$. All ring sheaves, module sheaves, and the object and morphism sets of $I$ lie in $w$; the site universes may differ from $w$.

source.place: Agent assembly from Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits: module colimits) and Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits, item (2)); the comparison for ring sheaves is not stated there as a single lemma. The multiplication-on-the-module-colimit argument is supplied in report.md.

proof.text: The scalar compatibility makes all $a_{ij}$ and $q_i$ morphisms of $R$-module sheaves: for example $a_{ij}(s_i(r)x)=s_j(r)a_{ij}(x)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], form a colimit $(L,(b_i:A_i\to L))$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$. Its existence applies in the coefficient universe after choosing a $w$-small site skeleton; the hypothesis of essential smallness guarantees sheafification there. Thus a map of module sheaves out of $L$ is determined by its composites with every $b_i$. The module cocone $q_i$ induces a unique $R$-linear map $u:L\to A$ with $u b_i=q_i$. We will construct a ring structure on this very $L$, then use the given ring-colimit property of $A$ to prove $u$ invertible.

source.place: Agent argument using Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2), and the tensor construction in Section 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text:
For $i,j\in I$, choose $k\ge i,j$. Multiplication in $A_k$ is $R$-bilinear for the action through $s_k$, so the formula
$$c_{ij}(x\otimes y)=b_k\bigl(a_{ik}(x)a_{jk}(y)\bigr)$$
defines a morphism $c_{ij}:A_i\otimes_R A_j\to L$. Here the formula is first a map from the sectionwise presheaf tensor, then extends uniquely to its module sheafification by [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. If $k'$ is another upper bound, choose $h\ge k,k'$; applying $b_h a_{kh}=b_k$ and multiplicativity of $a_{kh}$ identifies both formulas with $b_h(a_{ih}(x)a_{jh}(y))$. Thus $c_{ij}$ is independent of the choice. For $i\le i'$ the same calculation in a common upper bound gives $c_{i'j}(a_{ii'}\otimes1)=c_{ij}$, and likewise in $j$. These are equalities of sheaf maps because they agree on the sectionwise tensor generators before sheafification.

source.place: Agent argument using Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2), and the tensor construction in Section 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] twice to the compatible maps $c_{ij}$. The required preservation in the first variable follows from the balanced swap $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$, whose inverse is the same swap, for the tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. First, for each $j$, obtain $d_j:L\otimes_R A_j\to L$ with $d_j(b_i\otimes1)=c_{ij}$. Compatibility of the $d_j$ follows by this same colimit uniqueness after precomposing every $b_i\otimes1$. Second, obtain a unique $\mu:L\otimes_R L\to L$ with $\mu(1\otimes b_j)=d_j$. In particular $\mu(b_i\otimes b_j)=c_{ij}$. Moreover, equality of two maps out of $L\otimes_R L$ can be checked after all $b_i\otimes b_j$: first fix $j$ and use the first-variable colimit uniqueness, then use the second-variable uniqueness. All the diagrams used here have index $I$ in $w$, as the tensor-preservation statement requires.

source.place: Agent argument using Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2), and the tensor construction in Section 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text: Fix $i_0\in I$ and put $e=b_{i_0}(1)\in L(U)$ for every site object $U$, with compatible restrictions. For any $i$, a common upper bound and the unital transition maps give $b_i(1)=e$. The multiplication $\mu$ is commutative: its two orders agree after $b_i\otimes b_j$ by commutativity in a common $A_k$, so step 3 gives equality. It is associative as well. Repeatedly use [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] in the three variables to check the two maps out of $(L\otimes_R L)\otimes_R L$ after $b_i\otimes b_j\otimes b_t$. For $k\ge i,j,t$ their values are respectively $b_k((a_{ik}(x)a_{jk}(y))a_{tk}(z))$ and $b_k(a_{ik}(x)(a_{jk}(y)a_{tk}(z)))$; these agree. The associativity identifications are those of the sheafified sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Finally, multiplying $b_i(x)$ by $e=b_i(1)$ on either side gives $b_i(x)$; equality on all $b_i$ proves the two unit laws on $L$. Bilinearity gives distributivity. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf $L$ is a sheaf of unital commutative rings, and every $b_i$ is a unital ring-sheaf map, since $\mu(b_i\otimes b_i)(x\otimes y)=b_i(xy)$.

source.place: Agent argument using Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2), and the tensor construction in Section 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text: Define $s_L:R\to L$ by $s_L(r)=r e$. For any $i$, $R$-linearity of $b_i$ gives $s_L(r)=b_i(s_i(r))$, so $s_L=b_i s_i$ and is a unital ring map. The original $R$-action on $L$ equals multiplication through $s_L$: after $b_i$, both actions send $(r,x)$ to $b_i(s_i(r)x)$. More explicitly the two $R$-linear maps $L\to L$, for a local scalar $r$, agree on all $b_i$ locally; equivalently the two maps $R\otimes_R L\to L$ agree after $1\otimes b_i$, by tensor preservation. By [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits], $u\mu$ and $\mu_A(u\otimes u)$ agree if they agree after every $b_i\otimes b_j$. In a common stage $k$ both evaluate to $q_k(a_{ik}(x)a_{jk}(y))$, since $q_k$ is a ring map. Also $u(e)=q_{i_0}(1)=1$. Hence $u$ is a unital ring map as well as an $R$-linear map.

source.place: Agent argument using Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2), and the tensor construction in Section 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text: The ring cocone $(b_i)$ and the given ring-colimit property of $(A,(q_i))$ now give a unique unital ring-sheaf map $v:A\to L$ with $v q_i=b_i$. It is $R$-linear for the original module structure on $L$: choosing $i_0$ gives $v s=v q_{i_0}s_{i_0}=b_{i_0}s_{i_0}=s_L$, and consequently $v(s(r)x)=s_L(r)v(x)=r\,v(x)$. Therefore $vu$ is a map of $R$-module sheaves, and $(vu)b_i=b_i$ for every $i$; module-colimit uniqueness implies $vu=1_L$. Both $uv$ and $1_A$ are unital ring-sheaf maps and have composite $q_i$ with every $q_i$; the given ring-colimit uniqueness implies $uv=1_A$. Thus $u$ is an isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves, carrying exactly the legs $b_i$ to $q_i$.

source.place: Agent argument using Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits), Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), item (2), and the tensor construction in Section 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text: For a module cocone $f_i:A_i\to M$, let $g:L\to M$ be its unique factorization through the module colimit. Then $f=gv:A\to M$ is $R$-linear and $fq_i=gb_i=f_i$. If another $R$-linear map $f':A\to M$ has the same composites, $f'u$ and $g$ agree on all $b_i$, so $f'u=g$ and $f'=gv$. This proves existence and uniqueness for the specified cocone, as claimed.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q149-a7ffa91f5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS: I read the item and all 7 steps in full, plus every cited statement: lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful clause (2), lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category and def-weil-pbc-category-colimit. I checked them against Stacks sites-modules.tex 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits, l.1358), 03EP(2) (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits, l.4001) and section 03EK. The statement is unchanged and matches its use in step 3 of lem-sfb-qlbar-flat. It serves the first sentence of the main-20261015 proof lem-sfb-qlbar-flat.proof.md (unit sk-prop-sfb-finite-extension-compatibility), and the chapter is untouched. Every step is correct: (1) the scalar compatibilities make a_ij and q_i R-linear, giving the module colimit L and u with u b_i = q_i; (2) the common-stage products are R(U)-balanced, extend through sheafification, and do not depend on the chosen upper bound; (3) swap plus 03EP(2) gives mu, and maps out of L⊗L are detected on b_i⊗b_j; (4) the unit e = b_i(1) uses nonemptiness, and commutativity, associativity in a stage above three indices, the unit laws and distributivity all hold; (5) s_L = b_i s_i, the R-action is multiplication through s_L, and u is a unital ring map; (6) the ring-colimit property gives v with v s = s_L, so v is R-linear, vu = 1 by module uniqueness and uv = 1 by ring uniqueness; (7) f = g v gives existence and uniqueness. Small cases checked: singleton I, R = 0, non-injective transitions, incomparable indices. Empty I is correctly excluded, since the ring colimit there is sheafified Z while the module colimit is 0.
